messages:
maya: quick check — after yesterday's kernel selector bump i see decode p95 spike on mid-sized batches (4-8) on a100s, prefill looks stable.

devin: ugh. any prefill vs decode breakdown?

maya: yes. prefill p95 ~68ms, decode p95 jumped 74ms -> 210ms for the affected shapes. profile attached below. kv hit rate looks low for those requests.

maya: ```
model: llama2-13b
kernel: fused_gemm_v2
seq_len: 256
batch_shape: [6,8]
decode_p95: 210ms
prefill_p95: 68ms
kv_hit_rate: 0.43
cpu_ctx_switches: +18
```

li: low kv_hit_rate makes sense if we’re splitting queues and not priming kv for decode-heavy flows. are these warm-start sessions or cold starts?

maya: mostly warm-starts but interleaved requests from different tenants. when token budgets are hit we see more coalescing, and that seems to push the kernel selector to a fallback path with worse matmul perf.

arjun: that lines up with the token-budget behavior: when bucket is tight we reduce grouping aggressiveness, which can create odd batch shapes that map poorly to the "fast" kernels.

devin: idea: introduce a tiny phase-holding window (phase_shim) for decode-stage requests — hold for up to 1-3ms to let additional decode tokens arrive and form a nicer batch shape. only enable when kv_hit_rate >= threshold. config prototype below.

devin: ```json
{"phase_shim_ms":2, "min_group_tokens":8, "kv_warm_threshold":0.6, "apply_to": "decode_only"}
```

maya: tested locally w/ replay: phase_shim 2ms brought decode p95 from 210ms -> ~95ms for the test corpus, but it adds slight penalty for single-token low-latency tails. tradeoff table:

maya: - p50 unchanged (~23ms)
maya: - decode p95 down 2.2x
maya: - small request p99 up ~18ms absolute (rare)

li: that's promising. would also like to try a complementary kernel affinity tweak: prefer fast_matmul kernel for the common mid-shapes during decode path, but keep a cap to avoid long-run slowdown if it misses.

arjun: +1. we should A/B kernel affinity vs shim alone vs both. also make sure fallback timing doesn't thrash if kv priming hasn't happened.

devin: i'll add a per-request telemetry tag: kernel_choice and kv_hit_rate_snapshot, and expose shim_queue_length metric. that will help quantify side effects.

ops-bot: note — canary window available in us-west-2 tonight, 10:30pm PT.

maya: plan for canary: (1) deploy phase_shim=2ms + kernel_affinity opt-in on canary hosts (2) stream telemetry for kernel_choice, kv_hit_rate, shim_queue_length, per-tenant decode_p95 (3) run mixed workload for 1h, then check regressions and cost. rollback if decode_p95 > 250ms or tiny-request p99 > 450ms.

li: also add a lightweight KV-priming probe in front of decode path: if kv_hit_rate < 0.6, allow a quick parallel prefill priming for same session id — should raise kv hit rate for subsequent decode tokens. small experiment only.

maya: good call. devin, can you wire the canary config + tracing? arjun, can you prepare the kernel-affinity A/B flags and experiment buckets? li will own the kv-priming probe. i'll monitor and collect traces.

devin: on it. will push canary config and include a small sync hook to record kernel duration per-step. sending canary now :rocket:

ops-bot: canary started: id x-9832; initial telemetry available in 5m.

maya: i'll watch dashboards and post an interim in 10m. thanks all. cc @eng-sre

sre-bot: reminder — add rollback playbook entry to the canary run (automated noop if manual rollback needed).

maya: added to canary notes. will update results thread after the 1h run.

devin: quick note: if the shim reduces p95 but kernel_affinity increases CPU ctx switches we might be swapping perf regression for host-level contention. keep an eye on ctx switches and GPU utilization.

li: agreed. telemetry will include cpu_ctx_switches per-request and gpu_utilization by host.

maya: thanks — meeting to review results 11:45pm PT after canary.
